title: Multipartite entanglement spreads
authors: Sylvain Carrozza, Johann Chevrier, Luca Lionni
abstract: The entanglement structure of a bipartite pure state is characterized by its entanglement spectrum, or equivalently, by the family of Rényi-$k$ entanglement entropies with integer $k$. Taking the difference of two such entropies defines a quantity known as an entanglement spread, that is monotonous under local operations, and that vanishes if and only if the entanglement spectrum of the state is flat. We introduce a multipartite generalization of this notion which, for a fixed number $D\geq 3$ of parties, results in a collection of maps indexed by pairs of $D$-edge-colored graphs (obeying some condition). Each member of this collection takes the form of a difference of two multipartite Rényi entanglement entropies, each associated to a local unitary polynomial invariant (known in this context as a trace-invariant), and is shown to be monotonous under local operations. We then argue that a previously introduced family of so-called hypergraph-tensor (HT) states can be understood as a multipartite counterpart to the family of flat bipartite states. Indeed, we first prove that, when $D=3$, a tripartite pure state is HT if and only if it minimizes a particular (infinite) family of entanglement spreads. Second, we embed the set of HT states into the much larger family of spectral hypergraph-tensor (SHT) states, defined by a new Ansatz we introduce. We then prove that HT states can be uniquely characterized as the minimizers of some fixed entanglement spread among SHT states, for arbitrary $D\geq 3$. We also investigate SHT states in their own right: in particular, we characterize their orbits under local unitary transformations. Finally, along the way, the asymptotic large-$N$ expectation values of a number of entanglement spreads are computed in the Haar-random state of local dimension $N$.
summary: This paper develops a multipartite generalization of the entanglement spread, a quantity used to measure entanglement structure in quantum states. It uses this generalized spread to rigorously characterize a specific class of states called Hypergraph-Tensor (HT) states. The findings provide a powerful, universal diagnostic tool for understanding high-dimensional entanglement in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper generalizes the concept of entanglement spread, initially defined for bipartite pure states, to the multipartite setting ($D \ge 3$) to characterize the entanglement structure of quantum states.
main_result: It establishes that Hypergraph-Tensor (HT) states can be uniquely characterized as the minimizers of a specific, generalized entanglement spread among the larger family of Spectral Hypergraph-Tensor (SHT) states for arbitrary number of parties $D$.
method: The authors introduce a multipartite generalization of entanglement spread, defined as a difference of two multipartite Rényi entanglement entropies associated with local unitary polynomial invariants (trace-invariants).
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on multipartite pure quantum states $|\psiangle$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with $D$ parties. The states are analyzed under local unitary (LU) transformations, and the framework utilizes combinatorial tools related to $D$-edge-colored graphs.
key_observables: Entanglement spread (a difference of two multipartite Rényi entanglement entropies), entanglement spectrum, and trace-invariants.
important_parameters: The number of parties $D \ge 3$, the local dimension $N$, and the indices defining the specific graph structures.
main_assumptions: The generalization of the vanishing spread condition from the bipartite case to the multipartite setting is central, and the analysis relies on the combinatorial correspondence between trace-invariants and colored graphs.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the multipartite generalization of entanglement spread, then proves the characterization of HT states as minimizers of this spread for $D=3$, and finally extends this characterization to arbitrary $D \ge 3$ using the SHT Ansatz.
why_interesting: The work provides powerful, mathematically rigorous tools (entanglement spreads) to diagnose the structure of multipartite entanglement, which is crucial for understanding complex quantum systems beyond simple bipartite correlations.
